messages:
alice: Quick check — uploaded a short recording of the new 'rules playback' sandbox in the routing editor. Trying to validate priority reordering, inline validation, and preview simulation. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/routing-playback?node-id=42
ben: :eyes: watching now. One quick UX ask — can we make the "Play" control persistent when you scroll the rules list? I keep losing it on long stacks.
carla: From eng POV, playback ties into the current rule snapshot id. Need an API param snapshot_id, and we should disable live-edit while a sim is running. Also prefer a 2s debounce on reorder ops to avoid thrashing the server.
dmitri: Copy note: when a rule is skipped in preview we currently say "skipped" — can we change to "not matched" to be clearer to customers? And for validation errors, show a tiny example input that triggered the failure.
eva: A11y: keyboard nav for reordering — draggable handles need role=button and aria-grabbed states. Also we should announce when playback starts/ends via a live region.
alice: Good points. Ben — design alt for persistent play attached here: https://www.figma.com/proto/abcd1234/persistent-play
Also drafted a sample validation message to discuss:
``
Validation failed: Rule order conflict. Rule 'urgent' will never match because a higher priority rule matches all traffic.
Suggestion: Move 'urgent' above 'catch-all' or add condition 'user.header:X'.
```
Thoughts?
ben: Prefer a shorter, less modal-y line. Maybe:
"Rule ordering conflict — "urgent" never matches. Move above "catch-all" or narrow condition."
carla: Implementation nit: we can detect "will never match" statically using a simplified boolean satisfiability check over conditions. Might be expensive for very large rule sets; propose server-side check with a 300ms throttle and incremental rechecks.
dmitri: For preview simulation: can we allow quick sample payload overrides and toggles for latency/cost profiles? Also would be super helpful to have a tiny timeline that shows which rule fired and why (per step) for debugging.
eva: Timeline is useful but could be noisy for screenreaders. Suggest a collapsed summary (e.g., "Rule fired: urgent — click to expand details") and an "expand details" control that reveals the per-step items. Make sure the expand button is keyboard-focusable.
alice: @carla, if static analysis is expensive, can we run it server-side and cache results per-snapshot? We want near-instant feedback in the UI.
carla: Yes — server compute + per-snapshot cache makes sense. Fallback to a lightweight client check for very small rule sets. Will add cache headers and an incremental invalidation strategy.
sim-bot: Simulation job queued (job_id=sim-7723). ETA ~3s.
ben: :thumbsup: for the cache approach. One more micro-ux: highlight the rule that matched in the editor preview with an orange left bar for 1.5s so people can visually correlate.
dmitri: Quick product question: what happens if someone edits rules while a sim is running? Should the sim auto-cancel or keep running against the old snapshot? I vote auto-cancel with a small toast: "Simulation canceled due to edits. Run again to test new snapshot."
alice: Agree cancel + toast + a "Run again" CTA. Also add an analytics event 'simulate.cancelled.edit'.
eva: Also ensure cancellations are announced via the live region for screenreader users.
carla: I'll stub the server API: POST /simulate?snapshot_id=... returns an events stream and supports cancel tokens. Will add server-side cache + cancelation semantics.
alice: Thanks all — I'll iterate mocks and update the PR. Action items: ben — persistent play mock; eva — accessibility checklist + live region copy; carla — server caching + cancel; dmitri — sample payload UI + timeline toggle. Ping me by EOD tomorrow. :coffee:
